decisions.why: ICD s10 change process: a daughter that cannot meet it raises a blocking issue against LUM-CAR-A, it does not implement a variant

decisions.what: Common footprint adopted from ICD s7.1: 100.0 x 80.0 mm, R3.0 corners, 5x M3 (4 corners at 5 mm inset + H5 at (46,74)), 1.6 mm FR4, with a mandatory 30x26 mm RJ45 notch at (6,0)-(36,26)
decisions.why: H1-Q4 closed the stack at 11.0 mm; the carrier's board-edge RJ45 is ~15 mm tall so the notch is a hard mechanical stop and the anti-180-degree interlock (ICD s7.4)

decisions.what: Re-baselined onto ICD rev A2 (copied from boards/lumina-carrier/architecture/connector-icd.md)
decisions.why: Two changes bind this board: (1) board-wide HV clearance raised 0.60 -> 0.635 mm per TPS2378 vendor layout guidance, daughters inherit it; (2) new s8.4 - the carrier's TPS16630 load switch has a mandatory 10k SHDN pull-down, so a daughter may assume an unprogrammed/crashed/reset/brownout carrier presents 0 V at J3, not 48 V. Rail limits s6.2 and mechanical s7.1/s7.2 are UNCHANGED.

decisions.what: LED stage stays on +12V (baseline); the P1 '48V is 16x better for dimming slew' argument is WITHDRAWN as an artifact of holding L fixed
decisions.why: Verified algebraically by the orchestrator: with L sized for the same ripple fraction k, t_rise+t_fall = 1/(f*k), independent of Vin. At 700 kHz / k=0.30 both rails give 4.762 us (48V only redistributes 3.81/0.95 us between rise and fall). That is 33.8x the 141 ns PAR-REQ-01 budget, so NO rail or inductor choice reaches the requirement by gating the converter - it needs shunt-FET dimming either way. The 48V branch therefore buys nothing on fidelity and costs 0.635 mm creepage, 100 V caps, bleed path and daughter-owned inrush.

decisions.what: Stackup JLC04161H-3313, 4 layers, 100.0 x 80.0 mm, 1.6 mm
decisions.why: Switch-node containment 11 mm above a live 2.4 GHz antenna (H1-Q8 made Wi-Fi a supported control path), continuous GND reference under jitter-sensitive PWM, B.Cu consumed by two reverse-mounted sockets, ~120 parts in ~45 cm2. No controlled-impedance net exists on this board.

decisions.what: Dimming topology: shunt FET per channel across the LED string
decisions.why: Closes the PAR-REQ-01 TIMING wall: TPS92515HV direct PWM floors at 200 ns vs a 141 ns requirement, but its shunt mode is spec'd 10,000:1 = 10.2 ns min pulse. Implemented T ~ 50-100 ns, 1.4-2.8x margin. The RESOLUTION wall (17 bits needed, LEDC caps at 14) is NOT closable on this board and needs carrier firmware dithering (CR-5).

decisions.what: Design point 150 mA/die, 4 emitter packages, 2S2P per channel; emitters off-board on aluminium MCPCB
decisions.why: Full white = 0.718 A on +12V, 4 % under the sustained ceiling and 2.8x under OCP, so the board is electrically incapable of exceeding its budget with every PWM stuck at 100 %. Off-board MCPCB because 1.6 mm FR4 misses the junction budget by 2-3x. >3 A conditional flag CLOSED (max 0.30 A/channel).

decisions.what: No fifth (amber) channel on rev A; fit BOTH ID mechanisms (ID_ADC bottom-leg divider + I2C EEPROM)
decisions.why: Amber dilutes an af envelope that full white already fills to 96 % of the rail ceiling. ICD s3.3 makes the divider and the EEPROM coexist rather than alternatives - the divider gives board type, the EEPROM per-unit calibration - so PAR-REQ-17 is met without spending a pin.

decisions.what: Q1 CLOSED: enclosure sealed with LED heat conducted through the wall (not vented)
decisions.why: Owner decision: keeps dust out of a basement/garage install over years, and the strobe run independently recommended the same, so both fixtures share one enclosure design. 3.21 W internal -> 38 C air. The wall-conduction path becomes load-bearing for the thermal case and must be written as an explicit testable ENC-x criterion, not an assumption.

decisions.what: Q2 CLOSED: emitter is RGB 3-in-1 + separate white discrete, superseding D3's integrated 4-in-1
decisions.why: Owner decision, taken knowingly against this run's recommendation. Deciding factor: the thermal case now rests on a published 125 C Tj max and 3.5x stock depth rather than on an ASSUMED 12 K/W Rth from a sole-source vendor publishing neither Rth nor Tj max. Retires the 20 K/W marginality risk this run flagged. Consequences owned here: PAR-REQ-15 white/colour fringing becomes the live risk; the entire sustained-power table is stale and must be re-derived; 145 mA/die is reopened.

decisions.what: Q3 CLOSED: PAR-REQ-01 met by hardware + firmware. Strict reading (5% perceived, gamma 2.2) binds.
decisions.why: Carrier firmware commits to PWM-domain dithering >=3-4 bits (CR-5 accepted). Shunt-FET hardware half stands as designed (T ~50-100 ns vs 141 ns). FIRMWARE DEPENDENCY must be named in the design doc so it cannot be silently dropped: without the dither the requirement fails by 4.4-8.9x and no hardware on this board can fix it. Dither must be PWM-domain, not 60 fps frame-domain - a 4.4% dither at 60 Hz breaches IEEE 1789 NOEL on its own.

decisions.what: Q4 CLOSED: same-reel sourcing; 24C32 EEPROM fitted but shipped empty; PAR-REQ-16 and PAR-REQ-17 to be formally amended with original text quoted
decisions.why: No measurement instrument exists today, so colour matching rests on same-reel binning. The EEPROM is fitted so that decision stays reversible. Amending rather than quietly failing PAR-REQ-16 keeps the record honest about what was changed by decision.

decisions.what: PAR-REQ-16 and PAR-REQ-17 formally amended (AMD-01, AMD-02 in requirements.md s0), original text quoted
decisions.why: AMD-01: a chromaticity/flux bin is not an orderable attribute on LCSC/JLC and the selected vendor publishes none, so the BOM line was unbuildable; replaced by single-reel procurement for the whole build. This is a REDUCTION in guarantee, not an equivalent - same-reel is an empirical correlation, a published bin is a contractual limit - so PAR-REQ-06 is carried at reduced confidence with bench verification. AMD-02: hardware (divider + 24C32) is fitted; the calibration DATA is deferred because no colorimeter exists for this build.

decisions.what: The RJ45 notch is the coordinator's to implement via a central board_init --cutout flag. This run does NOT hand-edit Edge.Cuts and does NOT shrink the outline.
decisions.why: Both daughters need the notch, so it is being added centrally rather than worked around per-run. The notch stays a hard keepout in constraints.json meanwhile. Coordinator will confirm the flag exists before this run reaches P5. Supersedes the OPEN-7 remediation (hand Edge.Cuts edit) recorded at H1; the OPEN-7 coordinate-translation trap under fixed-outline board_init still stands and must be re-raised at H2.

decisions.what: P5 outline procedure fixed: board_init --outline 100x80 --corner-radius 3 --mounting-holes 4 --cutout 6,0,30,26, then verify geometry against an expected area of 7212.274 mm2
decisions.why: Coordinator added --cutout centrally (commit 18613d3) so both daughters share it. Expected area derived here so P5 has a number to check rather than eyeballing: 100x80 = 8000, minus the 30x26 notch = 780, minus 4 corners at r=3 = 4 x r^2(1-pi/4) = 7.7257. The outline_origin translation is the trap that would otherwise silently misplace every keepout.

decisions.what: Emitter set: 4x XL-HD6070RGBC-A46L-BD (C22434861) + 4x XL-HD6070UWC-A4-BD (C48586656); 2S2P, 150 mA/die, 300 mA/channel. Headline 0.717 A = 95.6% of the 0.75 A ceiling.
decisions.why: Both live-verified via parts_search this session and spot-checked independently by the orchestrator. The headline survives the package change because BOTH packages publish identical Vf ranges (R 1.8-2.4, G/B/W 2.8-3.4), so the 2S2P/150 mA arrangement falls out the same way - a derived result, not a copy-forward. All nine power rows independently recomputed by the orchestrator and reproduce exactly.

decisions.what: 150 mA/die confirmed over 145 (H1-P7 re-derived, not carried forward)
decisions.why: Every genuine HARDWARE ceiling passes at both: 2.8x on the 2.0 A OCP, 3.4x on the TPS2378 0.85 A MINIMUM limit. The only figure 150 fails is the ICD 8.5 W total, which ICD s6.2 itself calls a firmware-governed average, not a trip. Flips to 145 if the carrier owner declares 8.5 W a hardware limit.

decisions.what: Sense resistor 0.75 ohm (not 0.68), nominal 275 mA/channel - the COMPLIANT value is the default
decisions.why: P3 found that 0.68 ohm with IADJ tied to VCC gives a +-5.6% threshold band -> ILED 284-324 mA -> 0.775 A worst case = 103% of the ICD 0.75 A +12V sustained ceiling. Orchestrator reproduced it and also costed the proposed IADJ divider: the divider tightens the band but lowers the threshold too, landing at essentially the same light (0.928 vs 0.917 of nominal) for 8 extra resistors - REJECTED. Compliant-by-construction is the right default because the stuck-PWM backstop is exactly the case where firmware is dead and cannot govern the average. Costs 8.3% light vs the H1 point. Reversible: BOM value only, zero layout impact, changeable to P9. Flagged for H2.

decisions.what: Shunt FET switched to TOSHIBA SSM3K2615R,LXGF (C22371361, SOT-23F)
decisions.why: Closes two P3 open items at once. Ciss 150 pF into the 150 R gate resistor is tau ~22 ns, so gate edges land in the tens of ns against PAR-REQ-01's 141 ns pulse - the previously selected part was estimated at 100-140 ns, which would have eaten the entire timing budget. And Rds(on) 580 mohm is specified AT 3.3 V, so it is guaranteed on at our gate drive rather than inferred. Also resolves the no-first-tier-brand-in-stock risk. Dissipation 69 mW at 0.345 A peak. Package is SOT-23F not SOT-23 - fp_verify needs extra attention.

decisions.what: Keep the THT reverse-mounted ICD sockets; REJECT the HC-PM254 SMD equivalents
decisions.why: ICD s5.2 derives its 0.84 mm pad-to-pad creepage from the THT land pattern (1.70 mm annulus on a 1.02 mm drill), and that geometry is the carrier owner's frozen number. An SMD land pattern changes it and would require the ICD to be re-issued. Two hand-solder operations across 8 boards is the cheaper side of that trade.

decisions.what: Re-synced ICD copy again; daughters MUST use a 1.70 mm annulus on the connector pads (1.10 mm drill, 0.300 mm/side ring)
decisions.why: The carrier's P3 library work corrected the drill from the assumed 1.02 mm to an actual 1.10 mm, and normalised J3's annulus from 1.80 to 1.70 mm so both frozen connectors share one land pattern. The 0.84 mm pad-to-pad gap and the 1.32x clearance conclusion are unchanged, but the annulus is now an explicit daughter requirement - this is a librarian/fp_verify checkpoint, not just a note.

decisions.what: 0.75 ohm sense resistor ENDORSED by the coordinator; C2934269 recorded as the explicit 0.68 ohm alternate
decisions.why: Coordinator: 'a margin that only holds while software works is not a margin.' Reversion to 0.68 ohm stays live as a one-code swap through P9.

decisions.what: CR-1 CLOSED: R206 = 4.7 kOhm, 1% REQUIRED (not preferred). LUM-PAR-A is ID_ADC code 2, V_ID = 1.055 V.
decisions.why: ICD s3.4 rev A3, NORMATIVE. Verified: 3.3 x 4700/(4700+10000) = 1.0551 V. 1% is required because adjacent-code separation is 0.353 V against a +-0.05 V divider error from 1% parts plus a +-0.15 V firmware window - a 5% part eats the margin. Cited by section+amendment revision, not the header (the header reads A3 while its own parenthetical lists amendments through A6). The strobe run found its placeholder was set to THIS board's code and would have shipped announcing itself as the par - the value is functional, not cosmetic.

decisions.what: CR-6 CLOSED by ICD s7.7 rev A5 (NORMATIVE): sealed + wall-conducted, internal air 32-33 C at a 25 C room
decisions.why: The carrier re-derived and reconciled. With the LED wall path WORKING only 1.894 W enters box air (6.8-8.1 K rise); with it FAILING 8.5 W enters and gives 56-62 C - which reproduces the rev A2 af figure to the degree. So the af number was never miscalculated, it was the LED-heat-stays-in-box case at a 25 C room with NEITHER assumption written down. The at figure WAS a genuine error, exactly as this run found. This run's 89-115 C Hoffman/Rittal figure is now recorded as the CONSERVATIVE BOUND and the ICD explicitly says do not average it. Budget: 10.5-12.5 W of box air at a 25 C room holding air to 70 C.

decisions.what: PWM allocation NORMATIVE (ICD s3.5 rev A3): LUM-PAR-A runs PWM0-3 on ONE timer, 13-bit / 9.766 kHz, with a 90 degree phase stagger. CR-3 (14-bit/4.883 kHz) is GRANTED and available opt-in; CR-4 (stagger) is GRANTED.
decisions.why: The prior ICD claim that PWM0-3 sit on timer 0 and PWM4-7 on timer 1 is WITHDRAWN - the carrier does not hard-assign timers; each daughter declares its own map and firmware applies it from the ID_ADC code. Three timers remain free for this board. The 14-bit option doubles the driver timing budget from 141 ns to 281 ns and makes firmware dithering physically reproducible - it costs camera-flicker margin and must be re-tested against a phone camera on the first prototype.

decisions.what: ADOPT the 14-bit / 4.883 kHz PWM mode (CR-3, granted) as this board declared timer map, instead of 13-bit / 9.766 kHz
decisions.why: It doubles the driver timing budget from 141 ns to 281 ns, which converts the shunt-FET timing risk from unverified-and-probably-violated into comfortable margin against the only switching number that exists (toff 150 ns typ). It ALSO doubles the LSB duration, which is what makes firmware PWM-domain dithering physically reproducible - spec-dimming s2.7 ranks 1 and 2 as a package, not alternatives. Cost is camera-flicker margin: band contrast rises from 0.61% to 1.23% at 60 fps (still under the visibility threshold) and 2.46% to 4.92% at 240 fps - and H1-P9 already recommends declaring 240 fps out of scope. ICD s3.5 makes the mode opt-in per daughter and requires a phone-camera re-test on the first prototype.

decisions.what: APPROVED library edits: J3 annulus 1.80->1.70; J4 annulus 1.60->1.70 and drill 1.050->1.100; inductor footprint swapped to KiCad stock Inductor_SMD:L_Cenker_CKCS4030; SMF15A accepted as-pulled with a note
decisions.why: J3/J4: ICD-01 s5.2 mandates 1.70 mm annulus on a 1.10 mm drill and daughters must conform - the carrier already normalised its mating DS1021 pair the same way (its lib/EDITS.md edit 1). Note the as-pulled J3 gap of 0.74 mm still CLEARS the 0.635 mm creepage requirement at 1.165x, so this is an ICD-conformance fix, not a safety fix - but conformance is the point of a frozen interface. Inductor: as-pulled land is 3.20 mm centres against a 2.60 mm datasheet land, a 0.60 mm error with pads hanging 0.40 mm past the body; KiCad stock at 2.70 is a strict superset of the datasheet land. SMF15A: 3.26 vs 3.00 pitch is a 0.13 mm outboard shift with pad size EXACTLY matching the datasheet - solderable, accept.

decisions.what: P4 schematic-block agents run at opus/high instead of the tier table's fable/medium
decisions.why: Fable 5 credits exhausted account-wide. The skill's own tier table ranks fable/medium ABOVE opus/high, so opus is the nearest substitution that is not the silent downgrade the spawn rules forbid; user chose it over a cheaper mixed or all-sonnet split with the drivers/thermal safety content in view

decisions.what: The power sheet owns ALL FOUR PWR_FLAGs (GND, +12V, +3V3, +48V_SW); every other sheet places consuming power symbols only
decisions.why: each rail enters the board through J3's passive pins on the power sheet, so that is the one honest driver; PWR_FLAG's pin is power_out and a second flag on the same rail collides power_out<->power_out and fails the erc gate

decisions.what: J5 entry-direction question CLOSED: S10B-PH-SM4-TB is SIDE ENTRY and is the CORRECT part - no swap-part
decisions.why: datasheet p3 splits the model table into Top entry (B2B..B16B-PH-SM4-TB) and Side entry (S2B..S15B-PH-SM4-TB) columns, repeated twice more for the THT and LIF variants: the entry code is the LEADING letter, and the B in '10B' appears in every model of the series. Side entry is also right for this board - the module mounts to the enclosure wall so the harness leaves laterally regardless, and J5 is on B.Cu inside the ICD's 11.0 mm mezzanine gap where a top-entry PHR-10 housing plus bend radius would foul the carrier

decisions.what: The /PWM0..3 nets MUST carry the canonical root-level names /PWM0../PWM3; preferred mechanism is exposing them as hierarchical pins from control, with re-spelling constraints.json to /control/PWMn as the sanctioned fallback if that is not ERC-clean
decisions.why: sheets.md s2 states these are the names the schematic must produce, and constraints.json.high_speed feeds SEVEN consumers (check_return_path, planes_gen, route_critical, rules_gen, stitch_vias, constraints_lint, netlist_audit) - a mismatch silently drops the jitter-sensitive PWM nets from every one of them, on the board whose hardest requirement is the PAR-REQ-01 141 ns timing wall. It also fails netlist_audit outright (missing_net is an error), so it must be settled before the root build. sheets.md is internally inconsistent here - it lists PWM in the INTERFACE net table while its own From->to column calls them control-internal - so the tie-break is which artifact ends up TRUE: name-match is required either way, and the hier-pin route keeps one uniform convention across all root nets

decisions.what: REVERSAL of the earlier P4 ruling: /PWM0..3 keep their real netlist names /control/PWM0..3, and constraints.json high_speed was re-spelled to match. The preferred hier-pin mechanism was tried, measured and REJECTED
decisions.why: the hier-pin route works electrically (netlist carried /PWM0 = J4-1 + R202-1 + U202-1) but is NOT ERC-clean: 4x label_dangling, because the root subgraph for those nets is wire + label + exactly ONE sheet pin and KiCad 10.0.3 requires a real connection point. Two probes settled the rule: a second same-named root label does NOT satisfy it (8 errors, both flagged), while one TestPoint pin per root PWM wire takes the identical project to 0/0 - so buying the bare name would mean adding four PARTS to the root, a design change rather than a stitch fix. Every other root net escapes this only because two children expose it. lumina-carrier never exercised it: all 70 of its root labels appear 2-3 times. Outcome is equivalent for the seven high_speed consumers, which match on exact name and do not validate name shape

history.GAP_for_timing_budget: NONE of the three logic datasheets specifies an output rise/fall or slew rate at any VCC - only tpd. MUST become a bench measurement at P8 against the 141 ns PAR-REQ-01 pulse - flag at H2.

history.evidence: BOTH datasheets print viewing angle as symbol 2Theta1/2 = 140 deg TYP in the optical-electrical table (RGB p4 at 350 mA, white p4 at 700 mA) and repeat Luminous Angle 140 deg on p1. Same symbol, same definition (full angle between 50% intensity directions), same value. Radiation plots corroborate (~60 and ~62-66 deg half angle).

history.fix_per_datasheet: ROFF2 from VCC (pin 2) to COFF (pin 1) in PARALLEL with ROFF1 from VLED, sized by Eq 8 tOFF_shunt = (dIL_pp x L)/(VSHUNT + 0.7) and Eq 9 ROFF2 = -tOFF_shunt/(COFF x ln[1 - 1/VCC]). Figure 14 topology.

history.note: three unsourced/miscited numbers in frozen ICD-01 s4/s5, found by extracting the CONNFLY DS1023 datasheet. None changes this board design, but all three are load-bearing citations in a frozen document and the carrier owner should correct them.
history.d1_annulus: ICD mandates a 1.70 mm annulus / 0.300 mm per-side ring and derives the 0.84 mm pad-to-pad creepage gap from it. The DS1023 datasheet publishes NO pad diameter, NO annular ring and NO mask relief anywhere. The annulus is entirely an ICD construction, not a vendor figure - fine as a design choice, but it should not read as vendor-sourced.
history.d2_600V: ICD s5 lists 600 V as the socket rated WORKING voltage. The datasheet states only Dielectric Withstanding Voltage 600 V AC rms for 1 minute - a hipot number - and gives NO rated working voltage. Harmless in effect (the binding figure is the male 250 V against a 57 V application) but the citation is wrong.
history.d3_3A: ICD s4 builds the entire per-pin current budget on 3 A/contact derated x0.60 = 1.8 A/pin. The datasheet prints Current Rating: 3A with NO per-contact qualifier. Per-contact is the industry convention and is almost certainly correct, but it is an inference, not a quote, and it is the base of the whole margin proof.
history.d4_drill: vendor recommends 1.02 mm drill; ICD mandates 1.10 mm. ICD wins and already records the delta, but the hole is 0.08 mm looser than vendor guidance for a 0.60 x 0.40 mm tail.

history.reverse_mount_unsupported: the DS1023 part-number code offers only S = Straight type, drawn as a TOP-side straight THT socket. No down-facing land pattern, keep-out or standoff is published. The hole grid is symmetric so the land pattern itself is unchanged, but PIN-1 MIRRORING, silkscreen side and courtyard are the designers call and must be handled explicitly at P4/P6 - this is exactly the mated-view check the ICD warns about.
history.stack_height_ungrounded: no mating header, no mated cross-section, no insertion depth in the PDF. ICD 11.0 mm (2.5 male insulator + 8.5 socket) CANNOT be confirmed from this datasheet; only the 8.5 mm socket term is grounded.
history.no_pin_numbers: neither DS1023 view carries pin numbers or a pin-1 marker - numbering must come from ICD-01 s3.1/s3.2
history.J5_side_entry: S10B-PH-SM4-TB is SIDE ENTRY (B-prefix = top entry). J5 sits on the top edge feeding an LED module above the board - confirm side entry is the intended harness exit direction at P4, or switch to the top-entry variant.

history.ROFF1_net: connects to VLED, which on THIS board is the /LEDn_A anode net running out to J5 - P4 must NOT mistake it for a local node
history.ROFF2_source: MUST come from the device own VCC pin (2). Do NOT re-source from +3V3 or any external rail - the datasheet warns of an internal COFF-to-VCC diode that can pull VCC up and start the device with VIN unpowered
history.ROFF1_value: 10k, NOT TI literal 8.2k. ROFF1 and ROFF2 sit permanently in parallel so ROFF2 also charges COFF in normal operation; TI text ignores that and the ripple would land 12% low. E96 exact root 9.53k has zero LCSC stock, so 10k is both correct and orderable. Revert is one line at P4 if disputed.
history.placement_groups: ch0-ch3 groups in constraints.json must gain the COFF siblings (C304/R305/R306 and equivalents) - COFF sits at pin 1 with a short GND return and the annealer can strand it otherwise

history.severity: HIGH - threatens the PAR-REQ-01 timing wall that H1 closed
history.correction: the orchestrator recommended SSM3K2615R partly on a Ciss x Rg estimate of ~22 ns. That estimate is NOT SUPPORTED and is hereby withdrawn as a claim.
history.what_the_datasheet_actually_says: toff = 150 ns TYP (at VDD 30 V, RG 50 ohm, VGS 0->10 V) which ALREADY EXCEEDS the 141 ns pulse; no switching characterisation at 3.3 V drive exists at all; no min/max on any switching time
history.undocumented: the internal schematic shows a series gate resistor PLUS a bidirectional gate-source zener clamp INSIDE the package - neither value is specified anywhere. That internal RG sets a floor on gate rise/fall that no external Rg choice can beat.
history.driver_side_also_unverified: none of the three logic datasheets specifies an output rise/fall or slew rate either - so BOTH ends of the gate-drive path are ungrounded
history.conditions_caveat: the 150 ns figure is at a 30 V rail and 10 V gate swing including a Miller plateau; our case is a ~7 V string swing at 3.3 V gate, so it is not directly comparable - but it is the only switching number that exists

history.icd_check_done: ICD s3/s5 puts the REAL pull-up on the CARRIER (10k to +3V3); R207 is only the local defined-when-unmated pull-up, so mated effective is 10k||100k = 9.09k today and would be 5k if taken. ICD rev A6 requires a daughter to sink >=5 mA with real load ~4.3 mA; the change adds ~0.33 mA, still well inside the eFuse 10 mA FLT limit. No ICD conflict either way - this is a tuning choice, not a compliance one
history.current_state_is_acceptable: narrow bands are in the FAIL-SAFE direction and still <=0.02 Hz against a 30-120 s module time constant, so spec-dimming R10 is satisfied as built
